title: NEB Class 11 Chemistry — Stoichiometry — 2023
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What is the mole concept? Calculate the number of molecules in 36 g of water.
questions.solution:
**Mole:** The amount of substance containing as many particles as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of carbon-12. One mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number).

Moles of H₂O = 36/18 = 2 mol
Number of molecules = 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ = **1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules**
questions.knowledgeNote: Molar mass of water = 18 g/mol (H=1×2 + O=16). At STP, 1 mol gas = 22.4 L.

questions.question: 4.8 g of magnesium is burnt in 6.4 g of oxygen. Identify the limiting reactant and calculate the mass of magnesium oxide formed. ($A_r$: Mg = 24, O = 16)
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — Balanced equation**

$$2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO}$$

**Step 2 — Moles available**

$$n(\text{Mg}) = \frac{4.8}{24} = 0.20 \ \text{mol}$$

$$n(\text{O}_2) = \frac{6.4}{32} = 0.20 \ \text{mol}$$

**Step 3 — Compare with the stoichiometric ratio**

From the equation, 2 mol Mg requires 1 mol O₂.

O₂ required for 0.20 mol Mg $= 0.20/2 = 0.10$ mol, but 0.20 mol O₂ is available. Oxygen is in excess, so **Mg is the limiting reactant**.

**Step 4 — Mass of MgO**

$$n(\text{MgO}) = n(\text{Mg}) = 0.20 \ \text{mol}, \qquad M(\text{MgO}) = 24 + 16 = 40 \ \text{g mol}^{-1}$$

$$m(\text{MgO}) = 0.20 \times 40 = \textbf{8.0 \ g}$$

The extra 0.10 mol of O₂ ($= 3.2$ g) remains unreacted.
questions.knowledgeNote: The limiting reactant is the one present in the smaller stoichiometric amount, and it fixes the yield of product.
